# Decision-conflict report

## Computed (declared-edge completeness)

(none)

## Judged (undeclared-conflict sweep)

- **judged-slg2-dc4-vs-slt2-dc2-functional-sixth-gate** [no-conflict]: Story dc-4 keeps nolintlint out of the gated set to honor parent dc-2. It then has the witness do nolintlint's work: it requires gated-linter //nolint directives to name their linters and give a reason, 'to the same effect as nolintlint's require-specific and require-explanation'. Parent dc-2 fixes the gated set at containedctx, contextcheck, noctx, errorlint and gochecknoglobals by owner decision on 2026-09-21. It says any rule left out of that set stays enforced by review until a later revision measures it and gates it. If the witness fails the gate on a bare or unreasoned directive, rather than only counting it, the story adds an enforced rule whose true-positive rate is unmeasured. That rule sits outside the fixed set and only avoids the name 'linter'. No exempts edge is declared against parent dc-2. The tension is weak if the witness only counts and discloses. It is also weak if directive hygiene is read as protecting the baseline's integrity under parent dc-3 rather than as a ground-rule check. (confidence 0.20) — The reason and naming rule implements the parent's own ac-4 (every exclusion names a path or a pattern and a reason, and a static witness counts the exclusions). It protects the strict gate's integrity under parent dc-3: an unnamed or unreasoned suppression hides a finding from the baseline. It is not a ground-rule check of the code, so the five-linter gated set of parent dc-2 is unchanged. The owner chose this effect on 2026-10-01 (ledger SI-328, SI-330).
